goal: Reduce repeated selected phase/source metadata queries within one current guard and close last-final-grant callback withdrawal without caching positive authority across operations.
procedure: Require actual typed selected source registry, permission policy and optional Claim authority on the same current read connection. Copy metadata services without replacing actual instance-mutated source/permission predicates. Memoize source/raw/immutable-action/current-head/Claim row reads only inside one invocation, with an explicit distinct-row cap. Resolve actual registered and canonical source-parent closure; execute actual policy predicates and Claim availability checks. Invoke fresh grant callbacks and optional current phase/control guard, then re-run actual predicates. Finish with one bounded UNION ALL SELECT of every actually observed scoped metadata row, preserving immutable valid-time semantics and current heads. Compare exact canonical body and digest with observations and refuse missing, duplicate, ambiguous, unexpected or changed rows. Run no authority callback after this query. Discard all sampled readers on return. Use the same terminal current-head fence in the existing authenticated history path to catch a final grant callback revoking an earlier original. The full initial history authorization delegates its final pass to the metadata fence after authenticating real private originals. Current-original-permission marker callbacks also end with this metadata fence.
authority: Actual independently authorized source-purpose grants and registered canonical custody remain authoritative. The terminal row checker alone grants no source use, read, disclosure or execution, and is not a transaction across authority planes.
validation: Eleven local phase-fence tests and fourteen history-fence tests pass with actual selected source/policy methods and real owner grant authentication on controlled SQL/log ports. Existing eight formation preflight tests also pass together. Tests preserve actual patched predicates; prove no original byte I/O, one immutable source-row lookup per guard, current denial between calls, final-loop revocation before original decrypt, Claim quarantine after a slow authority callback, raw row mutation, foreign scope/connection, strict missing/duplicate/unexpected rows and explicit caps. A new real XTDB/Kurrent integration test covers the exact UNION statement, actual source/action/head rows, an admitted fictional Claim and real owner withdrawal; local execution stops at unavailable XTDB, so physical query and unchanged comparison latency are pending CI. The full initial history path authenticates both originals before its final metadata fence; separate final-callback regressions cover that path and the original-permission marker. Existing comparison custody checks retain their real initial private authentication.
failure_or_lesson: Sequential fresh grant checks still have a final-callback race. A callback checking the last source can withdraw an earlier grant after that earlier source was checked. Repeating the loop creates another final callback. One terminal selected-engine statement after the callbacks checks every current head together. Naively copying a policy does not rebind instance-patched callback closures; preserve those callbacks and explicitly sample their actual scoped head/action rows rather than bypassing them for speed.
notes: Keep this seed in FloRA. No host model, learned artifact, synthetic behavioral target or qualified latency is generated. The final SQL query observes its actual snapshot and gives no lease after return. Each private backend operation retains its own fresh guards, and other authority planes can change independently.
